original_question: Let Y1 be the prime Fano threefold of index 2 and degree 1, equivalently the degree-6 hypersurface in the weighted projective space P(1,1,1,2,3) known as the Veronese double cone. Is there a unique orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions on Ku(Y1) under the action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(R)?
target_in_paper: Section 6.5, Question 6.32: for the degree-1 index-2 prime Fano threefold Y_1 (the Veronese double cone), ask whether Ku(Y_1) has a unique orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions under the universal cover of GL_2^+(R). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10326895/))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's official formulation. It identifies the correct variety Y_1, correctly recognizes it as the Veronese double cone, and asks exactly about uniqueness of the universal-cover orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions on its Kuznetsov component. That is essentially Question 6.32 verbatim. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10326895/))
missing_details: Specify the ground field. In Section 6.5 the authors say they assume the base field is C for simplicity, against the paper's global convention that everything is over an algebraically closed field and that the reader may harmlessly think in characteristic 0. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10326895/))

Define Ku(Y_1) explicitly as the Kuznetsov component, i.e. the residual admissible subcategory appearing in the canonical semiorthogonal decomposition of D^b(Y_1) for index-2 prime Fano threefolds. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10326895/))

Make explicit that 'stability conditions' means Bridgeland stability conditions on the triangulated category Ku(Y_1). Definition 6.11 is stated for '(Bridgeland) stability conditions.' ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10326895/))

Define 'Serre-invariant' in the paper's sense: a stability condition is Serre-invariant when the Serre functor sends it to the same orbit under the universal cover of GL_2^+(R). ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10326895/))

Keep the scope narrow: the paper asks only the uniqueness-of-orbit question for Serre-invariant stability conditions on Ku(Y_1), not a broader existence/classification problem for all stability conditions and not the neighboring Torelli question 6.33. ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10326895/))
refined_question: Over the complex numbers, let Y_1 be the prime Fano threefold of index 2 and degree 1, equivalently the Veronese double cone (a degree-6 hypersurface in the weighted projective space P(1,1,1,2,3)), and let Ku(Y_1) denote its Kuznetsov component, i.e. the residual admissible subcategory in the canonical semiorthogonal decomposition of D^b(Y_1). Is there a unique orbit of Serre-invariant Bridgeland stability conditions on Ku(Y_1) under the natural action of the universal cover of GL_2^+(R), where 'Serre-invariant' means that the Serre functor of Ku(Y_1) sends the stability condition to the same orbit? ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10326895/))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 6.5 rather than the paper's other headline results. After reviewing that for index-2 prime Fano threefolds Y_d with d >= 2 there is a unique orbit of Serre-invariant stability conditions, the authors isolate d = 1 as the exceptional unresolved case, recall that Y_1 is the Veronese double cone, and then ask Question 6.32 exactly in the form your draft is aiming at. The nearby context also explains why this case is singled out: the Serre functor of Ku(Y_1) satisfies S^3 = [5], so the uniqueness criterion of Theorem 6.19 cannot be applied, and the homological dimension of the heart of a Serre-invariant stability condition is 3. To make your draft fully stand-alone and paper-faithful, the only real additions are the base-field assumption, the definition of Ku(Y_1), and the paper's precise meaning of 'Serre-invariant.' ([pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10326895/))
